title: Security review - data residency & region pinning
summary: Customer concerned about EU data residency, region pinning, and sub-processor disclosures. Walked through Redwood's region pinning options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), cross-border processing patterns, KMS/encryption, audit logs, and SSO/RBAC. Agreed next steps: share SOC2/ISO certs, sub-processor list, KMS whitepaper, and schedule a follow-up POC benchmark in EU region.
topics: Data residency / region pinning (US vs EU)
RBAC / SSO integration and audit logs
next_steps: Alex Chen to share SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 certs and PCI/PHI notes by 2026-07-24
Priya Patel to share KMS / encryption whitepaper and sub-processor spreadsheet by 2026-07-24
Schedule EU-region POC benchmark with Liam for week of 2026-08-03 (Alex to send Doodle)
Customer to confirm legal requirements for cross-border processing and any required SCCs by 2026-07-30
action_items: Alex Chen: Share SOC2 and ISO certs (due 2026-07-24)
Priya Patel: Provide KMS and sub-processor details + architecture diagram (due 2026-07-24)
Liam O'Connor: Provide sample workload and throughput targets for EU POC (due 2026-07-28)

meeting_header:
Date: 2026-07-22
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Maria Gonzales (Acme CISO), Liam O'Connor (Acme Head of MLOps), Sophia Lee (Acme Dir Eng)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a minute... um, Alex from Redwood here, I'm the AE on this account.
[00:12] Maria Gonzales: Hi Alex, thanks. Maria, CISO at Acme HealthTech. We wanted to focus today's conversation on data residency and region pinning — specifically EU requirements and cross-border processing.
[00:25] Alex Chen: Great; Priya's our solutions engineer, she'll cover the technical details.
[00:30] Priya Patel: Hi all, thanks. Quick agenda: cover region pinning options, cross-border patterns, sub-processor list, KMS/customer-managed keys, RBAC/SSO, and audit logs. Then Q&A.
[00:42] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. For context, our main concern is that PHI-derived embeddings and inference must remain in EU datacenters — we cannot have any customer data egress to US unless contractually allowed.
[00:55] Priya Patel: Understood. So Redwood offers three deployment modes: hosted (multi-region), dedicated (reserved capacity, region pinning possible), and private (VPC/on-prem). For strict residency we typically recommend Dedicated with region pinning or Private if you need full on-prem isolation.
[01:10] Sophia Lee: What's the difference operationally between dedicated and private for residency?
[01:18] Priya Patel: Dedicated gives you a dedicated GPU pool in the region (e.g., eu-west-1), data plane stays in the region and is isolated from other tenants. Control plane is still Redwood-managed but can be region-limited; Private pushes the control plane into your VPC or on-prem for full network isolation — more work to deploy but maximum control.
[01:35] Maria Gonzales: Is there any case where logs or backups still go outside the region? We need full audit trail stored in EU.
[01:44] Alex Chen: Good question. For Dedicated we can configure audit log storage to an EU bucket. Backups by default are region-local, but we have optional cross-region replication for DR; that would be off by default for these customers. We'll capture that in the docs.
[01:58] Liam O'Connor: What about metadata, e.g., model telemetry, kernel selection logs — do those get sent back to Redwood central telemetry in the US?
[02:08] Priya Patel: There's a telemetry stream for runtime metrics; for Dedicated we can either route telemetry to an EU telemetry endpoint or disable telemetry ingestion to our central metrics pipeline and provide the raw logs for your ops. There are a few toggles. Note: some optimization features rely on aggregated telemetry — if you opt to keep telemetry local we can run a subset of features or provide a privacy-preserving summary.
[02:32] Maria Gonzales: And sub-processors — we need the roster. Any third parties (cloud providers, monitoring vendors) that touch customer data?
[02:41] Alex Chen: Yes, we'll share the sub-processor list. Primary infra is the hyperscaler (we use AWS / GCP in region), and some optional partners for logging/observability. For Dedicated in EU it's typically AWS eu-west-1; those are in scope. We'll provide SOC reports for those as well where applicable.
[02:58] Sophia Lee: On cross-border processing, how do you handle requests that originate in EU but route to a model variant in US for capacity reasons — is there automatic fallback to US models?
[03:10] Priya Patel: By policy, you can pin by region and set routing policies. We have fallbacks for capacity but for customers with residency requirements we can disable cross-region fallback. If you keep fallback enabled we can annotate which requests would have crossed borders for audit.
[03:27] Liam O'Connor: That annotation sounds useful. Is that in the audit log?
[03:31] Priya Patel: Yes, the audit logs include route decisions, model variant used, timestamps, and region.
[03:38] Maria Gonzales: Encryption — keys at rest and in transit. Can you support customer-managed keys (CMKs) in EU?
[03:45] Alex Chen: Yes. For Dedicated we support KMS integration with customer-managed keys. For Private you manage keys in your own KMS/HSM. We'll send the KMS integration guide.
[03:55] Sophia Lee: Any limitation on tokenization or intermediate cache? KV cache for generation — is that stored in-region?
[04:03] Priya Patel: KV cache is kept in the data plane within the region; if you opt for cross-region features we'd replicate, but for EU residency we keep KV cache local.
[04:12] Maria Gonzales: Do you sign SCCs or standard contractual clauses for data transfers?
[04:18] Alex Chen: We can include SCCs in the DPA. Many enterprise customers require that. We'll get legal involved if we need custom language.
[04:25] Liam O'Connor: About sub-processors again — do you allow customer-side vetting or right to object?
[04:30] Alex Chen: We provide the list and a typical objection window; for large customers we can negotiate restricted sub-processors in the contract.
[04:38] Maria Gonzales: Audit logs retention — we need 7 years for some records. Is that feasible?
[04:43] Priya Patel: Long retention can be supported as an add-on; storage cost applies. We can configure log exports to your EU S3 bucket for long-term retention.
[04:52] Sophia Lee: For SSO and RBAC, does Redwood integrate with our SAML IdP and SCIM for provisioning?
[04:58] Alex Chen: Yes, SAML SSO is supported, RBAC with role mapping, and SCIM for user provisioning. We can show the mapping table in the tech docs.
[05:08] Maria Gonzales: Is there any personal data in debug traces or kernel dumps?
[05:12] Priya Patel: Debug traces typically include request IDs and timing; we scrub actual user content from the debug dumps by default, but if you allow deeper troubleshooting traces we can control their retention and scope.
[05:23] Liam O'Connor: What about subprocessors for model weights — do you host models with third parties?
[05:29] Alex Chen: Model artifacts are stored in our object storage within the region. We don't hand off model weights to third parties except for caching partners in rare configurations — we'll list those.
[05:38] Maria Gonzales: Can you provide a diagram of the control plane vs data plane flow for Dedicated and Private?
[05:43] Priya Patel: Yes, Priya: we'll attach architecture diagrams. For Dedicated: data-plane in region, control-plane can be region-limited but still Redwood-managed; for Private: both control/data plane in your VPC.
[05:55] Sophia Lee: If we choose Dedicated in EU but use Redwood's managed control plane, how do we handle support access logs — support engineers sometimes need to access customer logs for troubleshooting.
[06:05] Alex Chen: We can require just-in-time access with audit trails, and you can restrict who from Redwood has access. All access is logged and can be exported to your SIEM.
[06:15] Maria Gonzales: Regarding certifications — do you have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 for the platform?
[06:20] Alex Chen: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001; will send certs post-call.
[06:25] Liam O'Connor: If we run a POC, we want to benchmark latency and confirm no cross-border egress — can Redwood run the POC entirely within eu-west-1 with logs exported to our EU bucket?
[06:34] Priya Patel: Absolutely. For the POC we can provision dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 and configure audit logs to your S3. We'll need the sample workload and throughput numbers.
[06:42] Maria Gonzales: Any mention of subprocessors in the EU that may still route to a US analytics provider?
[06:48] Alex Chen: We'll flag any analytics partners and whether data is processed in-region. Most vendors offer EU-hosted options; where they do not, we'll note that and provide alternatives.
[06:57] Sophia Lee: On the contractual side, do you have standard DPA language and can you support additional clauses for health data?
[07:03] Alex Chen: We have standard DPA plus an addendum for PHI/healthcare that we've used with other customers. We'll share that template.
[07:10] Maria Gonzales: Any risks for machine learning model outputs containing PII or PHI? We need guidance on redaction and prompt engineering controls.
[07:17] Priya Patel: We advise on prompt design, output filters, and can add post-processing to filter PHI before sending responses downstream. For strict requirements we recommend on-prem or private deployment so output never leaves your control.
[07:30] Liam O'Connor: For encryption in transit, TLS — do you support mutual TLS for service-to-service?
[07:35] Priya Patel: Mutual TLS is supported for Private and can be enabled for Dedicated in some configurations.
[07:41] Alex Chen: Quick note: if you require CMK, for Dedicated we'll integrate with your EU KMS; for Private you keep keys entirely. We'll provide docs.
[07:50] Maria Gonzales: How about employee background checks and access controls within Redwood for EU data?
[07:56] Alex Chen: We have role-based access, minimum privilege, and run background checks for employees with elevated access. We'll include the personnel security section of our security pack.
[08:06] Sophia Lee: Any SLAs around data deletion when a contract ends? We need provable deletion within X days.
[08:12] Alex Chen: We support data deletion APIs and can provide proof of deletion and audit logs showing data purge events. For backups there may be a delay depending on snapshot schedules — we'll include timelines.
[08:24] Maria Gonzales: From a legal standpoint, we need clarity on subprocessors and a 30-day notification window for changes.
[08:30] Alex Chen: Standard is 30 days; we'll confirm in the DPA.
[08:34] Liam O'Connor: One more technical: rate-limiting and bursting — if you route EU requests to US for bursting, that would be a problem. So need strict pinning.
[08:43] Priya Patel: We can configure autoscale and burst policies to remain in-region; if extra capacity is needed we can burst within the same region or schedule pre-warming. Cross-region burst is opt-in and off by default.
[08:55] Maria Gonzales: Good. Any monitoring hooks for our SIEM — push logs or use a collector?
[09:01] Priya Patel: We support pushing logs via Kinesis/CloudWatch-to-S3 or syslog/Fluentd connectors. We'll provide the connector guides.
[09:10] Alex Chen: Recap: we'll share SOC2/ISO certs, sub-processor list, KMS integration guide, architecture diagrams, and the POC proposal. We'll also disable cross-region fallback for the POC and route telemetry to your EU endpoint.
[09:23] Maria Gonzales: Thanks. One ask: can you share a short note on how Redwood handles emergency support access and the approval flow?
[09:29] Alex Chen: Yes, we'll include the just-in-time access workflow and an example audit log entry.
[09:35] Sophia Lee: Ok, next step for us is legal to review your DPA and for Liam to send sample workload.
[09:40] Alex Chen: Perfect, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[09:44] Maria Gonzales: Thanks everyone.
[09:46] Alex Chen: Thanks all — we'll send docs and a Doodle for POC scheduling.
[09:50] [call ends]
notes: Transcript contains minor transcription errors typical of automated services (names, acronyms). Customer requested EU-only audit log exports, CMK support, and POC in eu-west-1. Agreed to share security artifacts and schedule POC.
